anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the USB receptacle J6's VBUS pin (A4) is wired to the global net 'VBUS', which is the same net as the power-mux U11 (TPS2121RUXR) output OUT (pin 1) and the buck input. Meanwhile U11's IN2 (pin 2) is on the separate '+5V' net. A second copy of the same J6 symbol on the Microcontroller sheet ties A4 to '+5V', so the single physical USB VBUS pin ends up on both the '+5V' and 'VBUS' nets, merging the pre-mux and post-mux rails.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the mux output rail is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux': USB VBUS must feed IN2 (+5V), and only the mux OUT should be the VBUS rail. The two nets must not be joined.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (page 7): 'J6 USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P' with 'A4 VBUS'; 'U11 TPS2121RUXR' with 'OUT 1 VBUS' and 'IN2 2 +5V'
Microcontroller sheet (page 3) right edge: 'J6 USB_C_Receptacle...' with 'A4 +5V'
note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: The USB 5 V supply is connected directly to the mux output / buck input instead of to the mux input, shorting IN2 to OUT. This defeats the seamless power-mux arbitration: with USB attached the 5 V appears on VBUS and fights the 12 V barrel-jack path through the mux, so the intended autoswitching between 12 V and 5 V no longer works and the two supplies can back-feed each other.

anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet the SPI nets are attached to GPIOs that differ from the firmware pin map: SCK (NET0019) lands on GPIO03 (pin 19), the three chip-selects (NET0016/NET0012/NET0010) land on GPIO02/GPIO04/GPIO05 (pins 18/20/21), and GPIO06/GPIO07 (pins 24/25) carry no net. Only SO (NET0014) on GPIO10 matches.
anomalies.expected: The specification fixes the SPI wiring as 'SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7', confirmed by firmware main.rs.

evidence.quote: Microcontroller sheet (page 3): 'GPIO03/ADC1_CH3 ... NET0019', 'GPIO02/ADC1_CH2 ... NET0016', 'GPIO04/ADC1_CH4 ... NET0012', 'GPIO05/ADC2_CH0 ... NET0010'; Thermocouples sheet (page 5): 'U5 ... SCK 5 NET0019', 'CS 6 NET0016'
SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7

anomalies.impact: If the firmware is unchanged, the ESP32 would drive SCK/CS on the wrong GPIOs and leave GPIO6/GPIO7 (the firmware's CS lines) unconnected, so the MAX31855 thermocouple reads would fail or read the wrong chip-select, breaking temperature sensing.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended design: the power sheet connects the USB VBUS pin to the post-mux 'VBUS' rail (the mux output) instead of to the '+5V' mux input, merging two nets the spec explicitly requires to stay separate and defeating the power mux; additionally the SPI bus appears wired to GPIOs that do not match the firmware's documented SCK/CS pin map.
